newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks descend at open after Dow tumble.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks descend at open after Dow tumble.

text.p: The Australian share market opened substantially lower on Monday as local investors reluctantly sold blue chip issues after a strong U.S. inflation report sent the Dow tumbling 148 points on Friday.
At 10.15 a.m. (0015 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 27.5 points weaker at 2,353.0.
The June share price index was down 30 points at 2,331 and at a 22 point discount to the underlying index.
Early volume was light with a handful of blue chip resource and industrial issues sharing evenly the burden of the correction.
"With our market it's not an aggressive sell-down, it's just a markdown," said Jamie Spiteri, a dealer at Sydney-based brokerage Shaw Stockbroking.
Spiteri said the pull-back was in line with expectations and trading activity remained very quiet as it had been for the past few weeks.

Dealers said the fundamental economic factors affecting the Wall Street market were significantly removed from the Australian situation and this was reflected in the market's fairly subdued reaction to the Dow's fall.
